Subject: Zenith Healthcare — exec authorization request: indemnity/warranty & pricing concession

Team — quick summary and ask: Zenith Healthcare is asking for a large commercial concession to close their enterprise trial. Key items in their redlines (attached):
- 35% discount off list for a 24-month commitment (we originally priced at 20% for a 12-month).
- Increase the liability cap to the greater of $3M or 3x annual fees (they propose unlimited for certain breaches).
- Broad indemnity language that includes third-party bodily injury claims (they want us to indemnify beyond IP/data).
- Extended warranty remedies — they want a replacement/feature-level warranty and SLA credits tied to clinical uptime.

I reviewed the commercial sensitivity: this is a high-visibility pilot with potential expansion into 150 hospitals (Zenith is a strategic early adopter in our target vertical). The customer is pushing hard on risk language because they operate in regulated settings and need vendor assurances. Procurement needs an exec authorization for any liability cap above $2M or changes to indemnity scope.

Attachments: Redlines_Zenith_v2.docx (customer redlines), Zenith_SOW_v3.pdf (current scope).

Ask: Legal and Deal Desk — please advise a recommended fallback: which redlines can we accept without exec sign-off, and which require approval? If exec sign-off is required, please flag the exact decision points and recommended limits so I can present to Marissa/Finance.

Lauren — reviewed the redlines and customer rationale. Bottom-line legal posture and recommended carve-outs: 

1) Liability cap: customer asks for effectively uncapped exposure on certain harms — we cannot accept uncapped liability. We can consider increasing from our standard to a fixed $3,000,000 cap (or 3x annual fees) for this deal given strategic value, but that requires approval at the VP level (Marissa) + Finance sign-off on revenue recognition impact.

2) Indemnity: we can accept IP indemnity and limited data-breach indemnity tied to our proven security controls. We must draw a bright line excluding bodily injury/medical malpractice claims and any claims arising from customer-controlled configurations. If Zenith insists on broader indemnities, that is a material risk and requires exec escalation.

3) Warranty/SLA: their ask for replacement/feature-level warranties and clinical uptime credits is too prescriptive. Offer: Standard warranty (defect remediation) + service credits capped at the liability cap for availability failures. Any SLA credits that effectively reduce our revenue or require escrow/retention will need Finance & Ops review (and escalation).

4) Pricing concession: a one-time 35% discount is steep relative to company discount bands. Recommend a structured concession: 25% discount on year 1 with an expansion clause and performance milestones (pilot -> 150 hospitals triggers additional discount). Any >25% needs Sales Leader + RevOps sign-off.

Recommended executive ask text to present: 
- Approve increasing liability cap to $3,000,000 for Zenith Healthcare only, conditioned on: (a) an indemnity carve-out excluding bodily injury and malpractice; (b) security attestation completed and cyber insurance proof; (c) a capped SLA credit schedule (max aggregate credits = the cap).
- Approve a one-time commercial concession of up to 30% (25% preferred) contingent on a 24-month commitment and milestone governance.

If you want, I can redline the document with the above positions and produce a short memo for Marissa.

-Markus
